entry.title: Platja de Sant Pol, Costa Brava
entry.summary: Platja de Sant Pol is a wide crescent of golden sand on the Costa Brava just north of Sant Feliu de Guixols, backed by a promenade and pine-covered hills. The water is clear and shallow, and a coastal path leads to the neighbouring cove of s Agaro. Restaurants and cafes line the seafront.

entry.title: Agios Georgios Beach, Naxos
entry.summary: Agios Georgios is the town beach of Naxos, a long strip of sand with shallow, calm water just a short walk south of the old harbour. Tavernas and rooms stand behind the beach, and the shallow water makes it a good choice for families. The beach is sheltered, though the summer wind can be strong.

entry.title: Baia Sardinia Beach
entry.summary: Baia Sardinia is a small resort on the Costa Smeralda in north-east Sardinia, with a sheltered bay of coarse sand, granite rocks and clear water. Pine trees and Mediterranean scrub rise behind the shore, and the harbour stands at one end of the bay. Boats leave for the islands of the La Maddalena archipelago.

entry.title: Mastichari Beach, Kos
entry.summary: Mastichari is a small fishing village on the north-west coast of Kos, with a long beach of sand and fine pebbles, shallow water and a gentle slope into the sea. The wind is often steady here, so the beach is popular with kitesurfers, and boats leave from the harbour for the island of Kalymnos.

entry.title: Praia da Fuseta, Algarve
entry.summary: Praia da Fuseta is a long, quiet beach of fine sand on a barrier island in the Ria Formosa lagoon of the eastern Algarve, reached by a short ferry or footbridge from the fishing village of Fuseta. The beach is wide and calm, with few buildings and shallow water on the lagoon side.

entry.title: Praia de Matosinhos, Porto
entry.summary: Praia de Matosinhos is a wide urban beach of golden sand just north of the port of Porto, with Atlantic waves and a long promenade. The seafront has a large collection of fish restaurants, and surfers and walkers use the beach all year. The water is cool and the waves can be strong.

entry.title: Agia Galini Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Agia Galini is a fishing village on the south coast of Crete, built on a hillside above a small harbour, with a beach of dark sand and pebbles beside the village. Warm water and a lively harbour with tavernas make it a popular base for trips to the beaches of Agios Pavlos and Preveli.

entry.title: Agia Pelagia Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Agia Pelagia is a small resort on the north coast of Crete west of Heraklion, with a curved bay of sand and coarse pebbles and a calm sea. Green hills rise on both sides of the bay, and a few tavernas stand along the water. The nearby beaches of Lygaria and Fodele can be reached by car.

entry.title: Almyrida Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Almyrida is a small village on the north coast of Crete east of Chania, with a long sandy beach, shallow calm water and a gentle slope into the sea. The beach is protected by a small headland and is popular with families. A few tavernas and rooms stand along the shore.

entry.title: Ipsos Beach, Corfu
entry.summary: Ipsos is a resort on the east coast of Corfu with a long curved beach of pebbles and coarse sand, backed by the road, tavernas and bars. The water is calm and clear, and the bay faces the mountains of Albania across the strait. Mount Pantokrator rises behind the village.

entry.title: Acharavi Beach, Corfu
entry.summary: Acharavi is a village on the north coast of Corfu with one of the longest beaches on the island, a strip of sand and fine pebbles with shallow water. Mountains rise behind the village, and the sea is calm in summer. Tavernas, shops and rooms line the main road behind the beach.

entry.title: Agia Anna Beach, Naxos
entry.summary: Agia Anna is a village beach on the south-west coast of Naxos, with a long strip of golden sand, clear water and a row of tavernas and small hotels behind the shore. A small fishing harbour stands at one end, and the beaches of Agios Prokopios and Plaka lie on either side.

entry.title: Platja de Portals Nous, Mallorca
entry.summary: Platja de Portals Nous is a small sandy beach on the south-west coast of Mallorca beside a large marina with luxury yachts, a short drive from Palma. The water is clear and calm, and the beach is surrounded by restaurants and cafes along the marina.

entry.title: Cala Ferrera, Mallorca
entry.summary: Cala Ferrera is a small cove of fine sand on the east coast of Mallorca, with clear turquoise water and pine trees on the slopes above. The cove is sheltered and the water is calm, and the nearby coves of Cala Serena and Cala d Or can be reached on foot along the coast path.

entry.title: Playa de Colonia de Sant Jordi, Mallorca
entry.summary: Colonia de Sant Jordi is a quiet seaside village on the south coast of Mallorca with a small beach of fine sand and clear shallow water, and a harbour with fishing boats. Longer beaches such as Es Trenc and Es Carbo lie a short drive away, and boats leave for the island of Cabrera.

entry.title: Playa de Las Americas, Tenerife
entry.summary: Playa de Las Americas is the biggest resort area on the south coast of Tenerife, with several beaches of dark and golden sand, a long promenade and many hotels, bars and restaurants. The weather is sunny for most of the year, and the water sports options are many.

entry.title: Playa de Los Cristianos, Tenerife
entry.summary: Playa de Los Cristianos is a sheltered beach of golden sand in the port town of Los Cristianos on the south coast of Tenerife. The water is calm and clear, and ferries leave from the harbour for La Gomera. A promenade with cafes and shops runs along the shore.

entry.title: Playa de El Medano, Tenerife
entry.summary: El Medano is a seaside town on the south-east coast of Tenerife, with a long beach of golden sand beside the volcanic cone of Montana Roja. Steady winds make it one of the best places in Europe for windsurfing and kitesurfing. The town has a relaxed feel with cafes and surf shops.

entry.title: Playa de Mogan, Gran Canaria
entry.summary: Playa de Mogan is a small beach of golden sand beside the harbour of Puerto de Mogan, a village of white houses, flowers and canals on the south-west coast of Gran Canaria. The water is calm and clear, and the harbour has cafes, shops and a weekly market.

entry.title: Playa del Ingles, Gran Canaria
entry.summary: Playa del Ingles is a wide beach of golden sand on the south coast of Gran Canaria, next to the large dune field of Maspalomas. The sea has strong waves and currents in places, and lifeguards mark the safest areas. Hotels, restaurants and shops stand behind the beach.

entry.title: Playa de Amadores, Gran Canaria
entry.summary: Playa de Amadores is a curved bay of white sand on the south-west coast of Gran Canaria, protected by breakwaters that keep the water calm and clear. Low cliffs and holiday apartments surround the bay. The beach is popular with families and is easy to reach from the nearby resorts.

entry.title: Costa Calma Beach, Fuerteventura
entry.summary: Costa Calma is a resort on the south of Fuerteventura with a wide beach of golden sand that runs for kilometres along the Sotavento coast. The sea is shallow and calm in places, and the wind is steady, which makes it popular for windsurfing and kitesurfing. Low hills and dry land lie behind the beach.

entry.title: Zivogosce Beach, Makarska Riviera
entry.summary: Zivogosce is a seaside village on the Makarska Riviera with a long beach of small pebbles, pine trees along the shore and the Biokovo mountains rising behind. The water is clear and calm, and the village has a relaxed feel with a small harbour and a walking promenade.

entry.title: Drvenik Beach, Dalmatia
entry.summary: Drvenik is a village at the southern end of the Makarska Riviera in Dalmatia, with a long pebble beach below pine trees and a view of the island of Hvar and the Peljesac peninsula. The water is clear and calm, and the beach is quieter than the busy resorts farther north. Ferries leave from the village for the island of Hvar.

entry.title: Marsaskala Bay, Malta
entry.summary: Marsaskala is a fishing village on a long narrow bay in the south-east of Malta, with colourful boats in the water, a promenade and a small town beach. The shore is mainly rocky, and swimmers use steps and a small sandy area. Cafes and restaurants line the waterfront.

entry.title: Ada Bojana Beach, Montenegro
entry.summary: Ada Bojana is a triangular island formed by the mouth of the Bojana river at the border with Albania, with a long beach of dark golden sand on the sea side. Wooden beach restaurants and a naturist area stand on the island, and fishermen use old stilt huts on the river. The sea is shallow and warm.

entry.title: Rafailovici Beach, Budva Riviera
entry.summary: Rafailovici is a seaside village on the Budva Riviera with a long beach of small pebbles and a promenade that leads to the neighbouring village of Becici. The water is clear and deep blue, and green hills rise behind the shore. Cafes and restaurants line the beach.

entry.title: Lalzit Bay Beach, Albania
entry.summary: Lalzit Bay is a long curve of sandy beach on the Adriatic coast north of Durres, with calm shallow water and a view of the hills behind the bay. New hotels, beach bars and pine trees line the shore. It is a short drive from Tirana airport and from the capital.

entry.title: Golem Beach, Albania
entry.summary: Golem is a wide beach of dark golden sand on the Adriatic coast of Albania between Durres and Kavaje, with shallow water and a long gentle slope into the sea. A strip of hotels, cafes and pine trees lies behind the sand, and the beach is popular with Albanian families in summer.

entry.title: Palasa Beach, Albanian Riviera
entry.summary: Palasa is a long beach of white pebbles at the foot of the Llogara mountains on the Albanian Riviera, facing the Ionian Sea. The water is clear and deep blue, and the mountain road above gives wide views of the coast. The beach is quiet compared with the busier resorts farther south.
